class_name: 否定-無意味-テモシカタガナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

glosses: even if …, it can't be helped
patterns.usage_note: Concessive 〜ても plus 仕方ない: doing or feeling this changes nothing, so let it go. It is the level-headed member of the family — 仕方ない stays respectable in writing, while its sibling しょうがない is markedly casual — and the たって／だって variants shift it toward speech. Do not confuse it with 〜てしかたがない (no も), which means 'unbearably'.

examples.ruby: 終[お]わったことをいつまでも悔[く]やんでも仕方[しかた]ない。
examples.english: There's no use going on regretting what's already done.

examples.ruby: 電車[でんしゃ]の遅[おく]れに腹[はら]を立[た]てても仕方[しかた]がない。
examples.english: Getting angry at a delayed train gets you nowhere.

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]に洗濯物[せんたくもの]を干[ほ]しても仕方[しかた]ないよ。
examples.english: There's no point hanging the washing out on a rainy day.

glosses: nothing to be done even if …
patterns.usage_note: The same verdict as でもしかたない — the action changes nothing — but built on 仕様がない, and the たって／だって shape is more casual still than ても／でも. 仕様がない contracts to しょうがない; the difference from 仕方ない is register, not meaning — しょうがない is the spoken form and, like 仕方ない, also stands alone as a resigned 'oh well'. The separate 〜てしょうがない, without も, means 'unbearably' and is a different pattern.

examples.ruby: そんなに急[せ]かしたってしょうがないよ。
examples.english: Rushing me like that isn't going to speed anything up.

examples.ruby: 悩[なや]みを一人[ひとり]で抱[かか]え込[こ]んだってしょうがない。
examples.english: Bottling your worries up on your own gets you nowhere.

examples.ruby: 壊[こわ]れたパソコンを叩[たた]いたってしようがない。
examples.english: Whacking the dead laptop isn't going to bring it back.
